rationale: B wins because it most precisely identifies the intentional input lockout, requires interruption from the current visible presentation value without snap-back, specifies monotonic sampling and CSS px/s velocity, carries that velocity into settling, bounds the projected endpoint before snap selection, and preserves product-defined target semantics. It also covers pointer capture, grab offset, one-to-one tracking, transform ownership, transition-all, Reduced Motion, and a compact validation plan. C is nearly as technically complete but exceeds the requested line budget; A is actionable but omits the decisive presentation-value interruption flow and a unitful projected-endpoint model.

results.label: A
results.summary: Strong static audit of drag anchoring, pointer lifecycle, motion properties, and Reduced Motion, but it largely misses normal mid-settle interruption from the current presentation value and lacks unitful velocity projection.

results.label: B
results.summary: The most complete and concise response: it covers all required gesture mechanics, presentation-value interruption, unitful velocity and bounded projection, transform ownership, Reduced Motion, and a minimal runtime plan.

results.label: C
results.summary: Technically comprehensive on interruption, velocity, transforms, motion necessity, and accessibility, but materially overlong for the 150-line constraint and less tightly scoped than B.
